examples.name: Basic table (columns + data)
examples.jsx:
<Table
  caption="Team members"
  getRowId={(m) => m.id}
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true },
    { key: 'role', header: 'Role' },
    { key: 'joined', header: 'Joined', align: 'end' },
  ]}
  data={members}
/>

examples.name: Identifier as a strong Link; a status in a Label
examples.jsx:
<Table
  caption="Team members"
  getRowId={(m) => m.id}
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true, emphasis: 'strong', render: (m) => (
      <Link href={`/members/${m.id}`} emphasis="strong">{m.name}</Link>
    ) },
    { key: 'status', header: 'Status', render: (m) => <Label tone={m.status === 'Active' ? 'success' : 'default'}>{m.status}</Label> },
  ]}
  data={members}
/>

examples.name: Selectable with a bulk-actions bar
Client-side pagination + sort
examples.jsx:
<Table
  caption="Team members"
  getRowId={(m) => m.id}
  columns={columns}
  data={members}
  defaultSort={{ columnKey: 'name', direction: 'asc' }}
  pageSize={10}
/>

examples.name: Server-driven (manual sort + pagination)
examples.jsx:
<Table
  caption="Orders"
  getRowId={(o) => o.id}
  columns={columns}
  data={pageRows}
  manualSort
  sort={sort}
  onSortChange={(next) => { setSort(next); refetch({ sort: next, page }); }}
  manualPagination
  page={page}
  pageCount={totalPages}
  pageSize={pageSize}
  totalItems={totalCount}
  onPageChange={(next) => { setPage(next); refetch({ sort, page: next }); }}
  loading={isFetching}
/>

examples.name: Full list page (header + toolbar + grid + pagination)
examples.jsx:
<Table
  title="All members"
  description="Everyone with access to this workspace."
  actions={<Button prominence="primary">Invite member</Button>}
  getRowId={(m) => m.id}
  columns={columns}
  data={filtered}
  searchable
  searchValue={search}
  onSearchChange={setSearch}
  toolbarActions={<IconButton appearance="subtle" aria-label="Filter"><FilterIcon /></IconButton>}
  activeFilters={role ? (
    <ChipGroup aria-label="Active filters">
      <Chip mode="filter" label="Role" value={{ label: role, sections: roleSections }} onRemove={() => setRole(null)} />
    </ChipGroup>
  ) : undefined}
  onClearFilters={role ? () => setRole(null) : undefined}
  selectable
  getSelectionLabel={(m) => `Select ${m.name}`}
  pageSize={10}
/>

examples.name: Empty, with an Empty State that says why
examples.jsx:
<Table
  caption="Matters"
  columns={columns}
  data={[]}
  empty={
    <EmptyState heading="No matters match" headingLevel={3} actions={<Button onClick={clearFilters}>Clear filters</Button>}>
      Try another name, or remove a filter.
    </EmptyState>
  }
/>

antiExamples.name: No accessible name
antiExamples.reason: A table needs an accessible name - pass `caption` (or a `title`), rendered as a visually-hidden <caption>.

antiExamples.name: Index row ids with selection
antiExamples.reason: The default row id is the index, which is unstable once rows sort or paginate - selection would attach to the wrong rows. Pass a real `getRowId`.

antiExamples.name: Baking domain filters into the table
antiExamples.jsx: <Table columns={columns} data={rows} statusFilter typeFilter /* invented props */ />
antiExamples.reason: Table does not know your filter domain. Pass your filter Icon Buttons through `toolbarActions`, render the applied filters as Chips in a named Chip Group through `activeFilters`, and filter `data` from your own state.

antiExamples.name: A data table for a card grid
antiExamples.reason: A dashboard of cards is a layout grid, not tabular data - use layout primitives, not <table> semantics.

antiExamples.name: Filter Chips without a named Chip Group
antiExamples.reason: Table lays out activeFilters but does not wrap them in a group. Pass a Chip Group named with aria-label ("Active filters"), so the filters are announced as one set and focus stays in the group when a chip is removed.
